name: Charminar
summary: The four-minaret monument built by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah at the centre of his new city of Hyderabad. Persian and Indo-Islamic forms; an upper-floor mosque is the oldest in the structure.

name: Makkah Masjid
summary: One of the largest mosques in India, begun under Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah and finished by Aurangzeb. Bricks made with soil from Mecca are set over the central arch.

name: Golconda Fort
summary: Capital of the Qutb Shahi kingdom before Hyderabad was founded. A granite hill fort famous for its acoustic system, the Fateh Rahben gun, and the diamond trade that passed through its markets.

name: Qutb Shahi Tombs
summary: A walled necropolis of seven Qutb Shahi sultans and their families, set in gardens below Golconda. Under a long conservation programme by the Aga Khan Trust for Culture.

name: Chowmahalla Palace
summary: Seat of the Asaf Jahi Nizams and the setting for state ceremony. Four palaces around courtyards; the Khilwat Mubarak durbar hall holds a run of Belgian crystal chandeliers. UNESCO Asia-Pacific award for restoration.

name: Falaknuma Palace
summary: Built by Nawab Vikar-ul-Umra and later bought by the sixth Nizam. Scorpion-shaped plan, Italian marble, a 101-seat dining table. Now a Taj hotel; grounds are guest-only.

name: Purani Haveli
summary: Official residence of the sixth Nizam, Mahbub Ali Khan, whose 240-foot walk-in wooden wardrobe survives. Now houses the Nizam's Museum and educational institutions.

name: King Kothi Palace
summary: Where the seventh and last Nizam, Osman Ali Khan, lived for most of his life and died in 1967. The monogram 'KK' of the original owner gave the area its name. Parts now a government hospital.

name: Badshahi Ashurkhana
summary: A royal congregation hall for Muharram built soon after the city itself. The walls carry some of the finest surviving Qutb Shahi tile mosaic (naqqashi).

name: Toli Masjid
summary: Built by Musa Khan, an architect at the Qutb Shahi court, on the road between the city and Golconda. Rich stucco work on the facade; sometimes called a smaller cousin of the Mecca Masjid.

name: Spanish Mosque
summary: Commissioned by the Paigah noble Iqbal-ud-Daula after travels in Spain. Octagonal spires and Moorish arches modelled on Cordoba, the only mosque of this style in India.

name: Paigah Tombs
curatorNote: Lesser known but beautiful tombs with intricate lime-stucco jali screens
summary: Burial ground of the Paigah nobles, who served the Nizams as generals and in-laws. Carved lime-stucco screens (jali) of exceptional delicacy, no two alike.

name: British Residency
summary: Palladian residence built for James Achilles Kirkpatrick, the East India Company Resident. Subject of the book 'White Mughals'. A World Monuments Fund project has stabilised the main block; outbuildings remain fragile.

name: Osmania General Hospital
summary: A vast Osmanian-style hospital block on the Musi riverfront, designed by Vincent Esch. Repeated demolition proposals after flood damage have been resisted by conservationists.

name: High Court of Telangana
summary: Vincent Esch's riverfront masterpiece for the seventh Nizam: pink granite and local pink sandstone, Mughal domes on a modern plan, on the site of an older Qutb Shahi palace garden.

name: City College
summary: Another Esch building on the Musi front, in the same Osmanian idiom as the High Court opposite. Began as an Islamic seminary and became a government college.

name: Kachiguda Railway Station
summary: Terminus built for the Nizam's Guaranteed State Railway in a domed Gothic-Mughal blend. Restored by South Central Railway with its cream-and-red colour scheme intact.

name: Hyderabad Deccan Station
summary: The city's main railway station, its long arcaded frontage a familiar face of Hyderabad in film and photograph.

name: State Central Library
summary: Founded as the Asafia Library, holding rare Arabic, Persian and Urdu manuscripts. The Indo-Saracenic building faces the Musi near the Afzal Gunj bridge.

name: Telangana State Museum
summary: Opened by the seventh Nizam in the Public Gardens; collections span Buddhist relics, Kakatiya bronzes, an Egyptian mummy and the Nizams' arms.

name: Telangana Legislative Assembly
summary: Built as a town hall to mark the seventh Nizam's accession, in white stucco with wide Rajasthani-style eaves. Legislature of Hyderabad State and its successors ever since.

name: Jubilee Hall
curatorNote: Near the Centenary Heritage Museum with remarkable displays in Public Gardens
summary: A pillared assembly hall raised for the silver jubilee of Osman Ali Khan's reign, still used for state functions.

name: Moazzam Jahi Market
summary: A curved granite market building with a clock tower, named for the seventh Nizam's second son. Restored in 2021; long known for its fruit, ice cream and flower trade.

name: Errum Manzil
curatorNote: Access restricted grand palace built by Nawab Safdar Jung Musheer-ud-Daula
summary: A hilltop Indo-European palace of the Paigah noble Fakhrul Mulk, with some 150 rooms. A 2019 plan to demolish it for a new assembly building was stayed after public protest; its future is unsettled.

name: Raymond's Tomb
curatorNote: Only French tomb ever constructed in Hyderabad
summary: A plain Grecian obelisk over the grave of Michel Joachim Marie Raymond, a French general in the second Nizam's service so respected that locals held an annual urs at his tomb.

name: Taramati Baradari
summary: A twelve-arched pleasure pavilion in the Ibrahim Bagh garden, tied by legend to a courtesan of Abdullah Qutb Shah's court. Now a state-run arts venue.

name: Hayat Bakshi Mosque
summary: Built by Hayat Bakshi Begum, daughter, wife and mother of Qutb Shahi sultans, on the old Machilipatnam road. A serai and step-well stood alongside for travellers.

name: Mahbub Chowk Clock Tower
summary: A Victorian clock tower beside the Jama Masjid and the old bird market west of Charminar, named for the sixth Nizam.

name: Sardar Mahal
summary: A European-plan palace the sixth Nizam had built for a wife, Sardari Begum. Long used as municipal offices and now largely disused.

name: Moula Ali Dargah
curatorNote: Home to several dozens of cairns circles that need to be rediscovered
summary: A hilltop shrine reached by about 500 steps, built after a Qutb Shahi courtier's vision. The annual urs draws large crowds; the hill also carries Qutb Shahi pavilions and tanks.

name: Bansilalpet Stepwell
summary: A large rectangular step-well cleared of decades of rubbish and restored in 2022 as a public space and performance venue, a model for the city's other buried baolis.

name: Secunderabad Clock Tower
summary: A 120-foot tower on the old parade ground of the Secunderabad cantonment, funded by public subscription and long the landmark of the twin city.

name: St John's Church
summary: One of the oldest churches in the Secunderabad cantonment, a plain Gothic hall with a battlemented tower and old regimental memorials inside.

name: All Saints' Church
summary: A cantonment church in coursed stone with a broach spire, its graveyard a record of garrison life in nineteenth-century Secunderabad.

name: Rashtrapati Nilayam
summary: The southern retreat of the President of India, built as the residence of the British Resident at Bolarum. Single-storey around a central durbar hall, in large gardens.

name: Mahbub Mansion
curatorNote: Historic Asaf Jahi mansion in Malakpet
summary: A garden palace of the sixth Nizam near the old Malakpet racecourse. Much has been lost to encroachment and neglect; a fragment and gateway remain.

name: Salar Jung Museum
summary: The one-man art collection of Mir Yousuf Ali Khan, Salar Jung III, a former prime minister to the Nizam, from the Veiled Rebecca to Mughal jade and a musical clock. The family's Diwan Deodi stood on the riverfront nearby.

name: Asman Garh Palace
summary: A castellated hilltop folly built by Sir Asman Jah, a Paigah noble and prime minister, overlooking the eastern approaches to the city.

name: Saidani Ma Tomb
curatorNote: Qutub Shahi era / early Asaf Jahi tomb near Hussain Sagar
summary: An extraordinary late-19th century Asaf Jahi mausoleum on the banks of Hussain Sagar, celebrated for its sublime blend of Mughal, Persian, and Qutb Shahi stuccowork and intricate Islamic lattice jali screens.

name: Khairtabad Mosque
summary: A 17th-century Qutb Shahi domed mosque and historic stepped reservoir built in 1626 CE by Princess Khairunnisa Begum for her royal tutor and scholar Akhund Mulla Abdul Malik.

name: Dabirpura Darwaza
summary: One of the few surviving gateways of the arc of city walls the Qutb Shahis and Asaf Jahis threw around Hyderabad; most of the rest were pulled down in the twentieth century.

name: Purana Pul
summary: The first bridge over the Musi, a run of 22 masonry arches built by Ibrahim Quli Qutb Shah to link Golconda with the growing settlement that became Hyderabad.

name: Afzal Gunj Bridge
summary: The stone road bridge over the Musi built under Afzal-ud-Daula, the fifth Nizam, that opened up the northern bank for the civic quarter of the twentieth century.

name: Bella Vista
summary: A Paigah mansion later used by the seventh Nizam's family, set in terraced gardens above the Husain Sagar. Now the campus of the Administrative Staff College of India.

name: Sir Ronald Ross Building
summary: The hospital building where Ronald Ross, working in the Secunderabad garrison in 1897, proved the mosquito transmission of malaria. Restored and marked with a plaque.

name: Husain Sagar Lake
summary: The vast artificial lake that divides Hyderabad from Secunderabad, built in 1562 by Ibrahim Quli Qutb Shah's minister Husain Shah Wali. Its shores define the twin cities' geography.

name: Mir Alam Tank
summary: A masonry dam and reservoir built in 1804 under the statesman Mir Alam, engineered by Colonel John Malcolm. One of the largest masonry dams in South Asia at the time.

name: Osman Sagar (Gandipet Lake)
summary: A major reservoir on the Musi built after the 1908 flood to supply Hyderabad with clean water. Named for Nizam VII; its construction displaced several villages.

name: Khairatabad Bada Ganesh
summary: Founded in 1954 by freedom fighter S. Sankaraiah, this world-renowned annual clay deity reaches up to 70 feet in height, drawing millions of pilgrims as India's largest and most famous community Ganesha idol.

name: HITEC City & Cyber Towers
summary: Inaugurated in 1998, the iconic 10-storey octagonal Cyber Towers building and fountain plaza transformed Hyderabad into a global technology capital.

name: Monolithic Buddha Statue
summary: Standing 18 metres (58 feet) tall and weighing 450 tonnes, this colossal white granite monolith was carved from a single boulder and stands majestically on Gibraltar Rock in the center of the 16th-century Hussain Sagar lake.

name: Ravindra Bharathi Cultural Complex
summary: Built to commemorate the birth centenary of Nobel laureate Rabindranath Tagore, Ravindra Bharathi is Hyderabad's premier performing arts auditorium and cultural heart, hosting classical dance, theatre, music, and poetry for over six decades.

name: Birla Mandir (Naubath Pahad)
summary: A breathtaking 2,000-tonne white Rajasthani marble temple perched atop the 280-foot high Naubat Pahad hill, blending South Indian Dravidian gopuram and Utkal temple architecture overlooking Hussain Sagar.

name: Telangana Martyrs Memorial
summary: Sculpted by prominent artist Aekka Yadagiri Rao, this 25-foot black granite monument in Gun Park stands opposite the State Assembly as the poignant memorial commemorating the 369 student martyrs of the 1969 Telangana agitation.

name: Premamati Mosque (Qutb Shahi Masjid)
summary: A pre-Hyderabad Qutb Shahi masterpiece in Ibrahim Bagh. Begun under Ibrahim Quli Qutb Shah as the planned grand mosque for a new capital that was abandoned for water shortage, it later served as the architectural scale prototype for Makkah Masjid.

name: Gachibowli Stepwell
curatorNote: 200 year old step well that lent its name to Gachibowli
summary: The 200-year-old limestone-lined stepwell that gave the entire neighborhood of Gachibowli its name. Once irrigated 10 acres of surrounding farmland; restored in 2021.

name: Amin Khan Tomb (1568)
curatorNote: Tomb from 1568 that is older than the Charminar
summary: An octagonal granite and stucco tomb built in 1568 by Amin Khan, high minister under Ibrahim Qutb Shah. It predates Charminar by 23 years.

name: Telunganaapura Inscription (Tellapur)
curatorNote: First Telugu inscription to contain the word “Telangana”
summary: A 1417 CE stone inscription that records the excavation of a public stepwell, recognized as the earliest known Telugu epigraph containing the word 'Telangana' (Telunganaapura).

name: Patancheru Jain Mandapam (Old Temple)
curatorNote: Historic 800-1200 year old Jain mandapam
summary: An 800–1200 year old Rashtrakuta / Western Chalukyan carved Jain pillared mandapam surviving in the heart of old Patancheru.

name: Sri Indreshwara Swamy Temple
curatorNote: 700 year old temple with hero stones and statues
summary: A 700-year-old Kakatiya-period stone temple complex preserving ancient hero stones (Veeragallu), Nandi mandapa, and sculpted Shaivite panels.

name: Hasmathpet Megalithic Cairns
curatorNote: Cairns, or prehistoric burial site, from 2,300 years ago
summary: Over 2,300-year-old Iron Age megalithic burial complex composed of monumental granite boulder stone circles and cist tombs.

name: Megalithic Burial Site (Kondapur / BJR Nagar)
curatorNote: Considered the oldest, 4500 year old Iron Age site
summary: Prehistoric Iron Age stone circle burials situated on a rocky ridge in western Hyderabad, estimated to be between 2,500 and 3,500 years old.

name: Vishnukundina Dynasty Brick & Stone Excavations
curatorNote: Remains of a 6th century Vishnukundina temple
summary: Excavated 5th–6th century CE capital ruins of the Vishnukundina dynasty, featuring brick residential complexes, fortified walls, and rock-cut shrines.

name: Ancient Shiva Temple & Hero Stones (Keesaragutta)
curatorNote: Ancient temple. Walk up the hill behind the temple to find more hero stones and some ruins.
summary: Ancient hilltop temple site dotted with monolithic stone Shiva lingas, medieval hero stones (Veeragallu), and boulder caves.

name: Shaikpet Sarai (Caravanserai)
curatorNote: Old caravanserai or resting place during trade routes
summary: A monumental 30-room stone caravanserai built during the reign of Abdullah Qutb Shah for merchants and traveling caravans between Golconda and Hyderabad.

name: Shaikpet Qutb Shahi Mosque
curatorNote: Old Qutub Shahi era mosque lying in neglect
summary: A graceful 17th-century Qutb Shahi triple-arched stone mosque featuring stucco relief and minarets, situated near the historic Shaikpet Sarai.

name: Sri Anantha Padmanabha Swamy Cave Temple
curatorNote: Historic 8 century old cave temple dedicated to Lord Vishnu
summary: An ancient 800-year-old rock-cut cave shrine dedicated to Lord Vishnu, nestled inside the prehistoric Khajaguda granite rock formations.

name: Sri Beerappa Temple & Petroglyphs
curatorNote: Hero stones found here, along with petroglyphs behind it
summary: A traditional Kuruma community temple site housing medieval warrior hero stones and prehistoric petroglyphs carved on rear boulders.

name: Forestrek Park Prehistoric Rock Art
curatorNote: Home to ancient rock art
summary: Ancient prehistoric rock art and petroglyphs preserved inside granitic rock shelters within Forestrek Park near Chilkur.

name: Gundlapochampally Prehistoric Rock Art & Caves
curatorNote: Cave painting at several sites, from 2000-3000 years ago. Also home to a lot of medieval Hindu heritage
summary: Granite hillocks housing 2,000–3,000-year-old ochre cave paintings alongside medieval Shaivite hero stones and cisterns.

name: Kondapur Stepwell (Baoli)
curatorNote: Old stepwell in Kondapur
summary: An Asaf Jahi-era stone stepwell in Kondapur that historically watered the local village community and agricultural fields.

name: Kondapur Archaeological Museum & Satavahana Site
curatorNote: Contains remains of a 2,000-3,000 year old large settlement
summary: An ASI museum showcasing antiquities from an extensive 2,000–3,000-year-old Satavahana urban trading and Buddhist settlement.

name: Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Cave Temple
curatorNote: Cave temple of Lord Narasimha with intricate carvings
summary: A 14th-century cave temple carved into the granite ramparts of Rachakonda Fort featuring ornate pillars and sculpted Narasimha icons.

name: Sri Rama Temple (Rachakonda Fort)
curatorNote: Beautiful ancient temple of Lord Rama
summary: An ancient stone temple of Lord Rama situated in the valley of Rachakonda Fort, showcasing classic medieval Deccan temple architecture.

name: Khursheed Jah Devdi
curatorNote: Unique piece of European architecture in Hyderabad
summary: A grand 19th-century neoclassical European palace built by the premier Paigah nobleman Nawab Khursheed Jah Bahadur.

name: Asmangadh Palace
curatorNote: Old Asaf Jahi palace
summary: A European medieval Gothic castle perched atop a hillock in Malakpet, built in 1885 by Prime Minister Sir Asman Jah.

name: Sri Ranganatha Swamy Temple (Jiyaguda)
curatorNote: Historic centuries old temple dedicated to Lord Vishnu
summary: A 400-year-old riverside temple dedicated to Lord Ranganatha on the south bank of the Musi River, known for traditional Vaikunta Ekadasi boat festivals.

name: Sitarambagh Temple Complex
curatorNote: Historic temple dedicated to Lord Vishnu
summary: A massive 25-acre fortified temple complex constructed in 1832 blending Rajasthani, European, and Qutb Shahi architectural traditions.

name: Malakpet 17th-Century Hero Stone & Pillar
curatorNote: 17th century hero stone and burial site
summary: A 17th-century inscribed warrior hero stone (Veeragallu) and sculpted Shiva pillar standing quietly in Old Malakpet.

name: BN Reddy Hills Prehistoric Lithic Site
curatorNote: Site where ancient rock tools were found
summary: Natural granite rock formations where archaeologists documented prehistoric stone-tool manufacturing sites and cupules.

name: Hill Fort Palace (Ritz Hotel)
curatorNote: ACCESS RESTRICTED. Grand Asaf Jahi castle on the hill
summary: A 1915 Tudor-style castle built by Chief Justice Sir Nizamat Jung, later official residence of Prince Moazzam Jah and home to the Ritz Hotel.

name: Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple (Nanakramguda)
curatorNote: Historic 200 year old temple dedicated to Lord Vishnu
summary: A 200-year-old temple complex enclosed within stone perimeter walls, featuring a stepwell, mandapa, and traditional dwajasthambam.

name: Wadakpally Asaf Jahi Watchtower
curatorNote: Watch tower from the Asaf Jahi era for military outposts
summary: A cylindrical stone military watchtower (burj) from the Asaf Jahi era erected for frontier observation and courier security.

name: Kakatiya Era Hero Stones (Veeragallulu)
curatorNote: Kakatiya Herostones (Veeragallulu) from the 14th century
summary: 14th-century Kakatiya warrior memorial stones (Veeragallulu) depicting heroic battles, celestial ascent, and divine worship in Kailasa.

name: Rameshwaram Banda Temple Ruins & Viewpoint
curatorNote: Contains ruins of a 14th century Kakatiya temple
summary: A scenic rocky granite ridge preserving ruins of a 14th-century Kakatiya temple and monolithic pillars overlooking the surrounding plains.
